review_notes: Reviewed all 426 lines of the target and inspected the Fourier definitions and multiplier uses in the related Leray sources, along with Mathlib’s Schwartz Fourier API. The proposed generalization follows that API’s stated domain assumptions; I did not execute Lean or claim the replacement was compiled.

findings.excerpt:
theorem fourier_postcompCLM
    {F G : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] [CompleteSpace F]
    [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℂ G] [CompleteSpace G]
    (L : F →L[ℂ] G) (f : SchwartzMap L2Vec3 F) :
findings.problem: The theorem is generic in its value spaces and postcomposition map, but fixes the Fourier domain to `L2Vec3`. Mathlib’s Schwartz Fourier API is stated for any finite-dimensional real inner-product domain, so this useful postcomposition identity is unnecessarily restricted to the library’s 3D coordinates.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the fixed domain with a variable `V` carrying `[NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V]`, and change `SchwartzMap L2Vec3 F` to `SchwartzMap V F`. The proof can use the same `Real.fourier_eq` rewrites and `L.integral_comp_comm` argument. This formulation includes the zero-dimensional case; no nonzero-dimension assumption is needed for the integral-commutation argument.
findings.benefit: The identity becomes reusable for Schwartz Fourier transforms on other finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, without duplicating its proof for each spatial domain.
